LESSON: TURNING EFFECT OF FORCE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Natural Physical Science
Topic 3.1: Turning effect of force
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Turning effect of force, part of Natural Physical Science in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How is the turning effect of force used in our daily life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use digital devices and/or print media to research on moments of a force at a point. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or use adapted digital devices to carry out the research. Screen resolution could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use digital devices and/or print media to research on moments of a force at a point. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or use adapted digital devices to carry out the research. Screen resolution could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light,
2. watch animations and simulations on moments of anti-parallel forces and discuss with peers. Learners with short stature and those using wheelchairs could require preferential seating for

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Turning effect of force together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner solves numerical problems involving both moments of a force

and moments of anti-parallel forces and identifies areas where moments of a force is used in day to day life.

● Digital literacy: as the learner interacts with digital technology when researching on moments of a force at a point

and moments of anti-parallel forces.

Values:
● Integrity: the learner displays honesty while using digital devices to search for information on moments of a force at

a point and moments of anti-parallel forces.

● Respect: the learner respects others’ opinions while discussing with peers on the examples involving turning effect of

force in daily life.
